assets.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Final title-background illustration for SHIPS, a serious adult maritime merchant game circa 1810 on an 800x480 monochrome e-paper screen. Wide 5:3 horizontal composition. A fully visible realistic merchant sailing vessel under white canvas sails in three-quarter broadside, substantial dark wooden hull, elegant functional rigging, on a calm open sea with a distant low coast. The mood is confident, contemplative and seafaring, like a fine nineteenth-century maritime book engraving, never a children's illustration or a toy. Pen-and-ink, pure black and white, bold crisp outer contours, restrained sparse engraving only where structural, large clear white sails and sky, 3-5 horizontal water strokes. Place the vessel from about x=35% to x=82%, y=25% to y=81%; its hull and every mast fully visible. Preserve a blank white upper-left region x=0..40%, y=0..28% for live title text and a blank lower-left strip x=0..65%, y=86..100% for a live start prompt. Rightmost 14% of canvas plain white for physical button legend. No text, lettering, titles, banner, border, frames, UI, compass, parchment texture, gray, gradients, halftone, dithering, pixel art, cute styling, anthropomorphic features or decorative pirate motifs. Finished illustration only.

Use case: historical-scene. Production game asset sheet for a mature maritime trading game circa 1810. Refined black pen-and-ink engraving with confident broad contours and a few deliberate structural interior strokes, realistic adult proportions, restrained detail. Pure black ink on pure white background; no gray wash, no halftone, no dithering, no stippling, no pixel art, no cartoon, no childish proportions, no gradients, no UI, no letters, no labels, no numerals, no watermark. Every subject must remain clear after reduction to a very small native monochrome bitmap. Give subjects strong, visually distinct silhouettes and generous white separation. Exactly TWENTY-FOUR isolated architectural illustrations arranged in a precise SIX-COLUMN by FOUR-ROW grid on a wide 3:2 sheet. Each equal cell contains one separate complete subject, centered with 12% blank margins on every side, no drawn grid lines or cell borders. The grid fills the canvas evenly, so it can be cropped into 24 equal rectangular cells. These are small working-port landmarks, viewed in consistent three-quarter elevation, no surrounding scenery or people. Row 1 left to right: (1) square harbor clock tower with slate roof; (2) grain mill with prominent waterwheel; (3) tall timber storehouse with stacked logs and loading slip; (4) two tall wooden cargo gantries; (5) broad spice-market canopy with jars beneath; (6) narrow landing jetty with a shelter. Row 2: (7) apothecary building with balcony and outside stairs; (8) open timber racks filled with cut logs; (9) tall grain tower with pitched roof; (10) squat coastal lighthouse; (11) stepped medicinal-herb drying terraces; (12) upright cloth drying frames. Row 3: (13) low forge with tall square chimney; (14) large tea-loading gantry with tea chests; (15) low coastal tea pavilion with wide eaves; (16) covered medicine storehouse with a broad roof; (17) three bottle-shaped porcelain kilns; (18) cloth suspended between two waterfront sheds. Row 4: (19) spice drying courts with baskets; (20) heavy iron cargo hoist with ingots; (21) modest clinic beside a short jetty; (22) timber log boom floating parallel to a quay; (23) two cargo cranes facing opposite directions; (24) coastal signal tower with a plain pennant. Exactly 6 columns, 4 rows, one subject per cell, all 24 visible and separate. Keep drawings compact and bold, intended for 64x56 output per cell.
